sources.entry: SwarmVault — Local-first RAG knowledge base compiler inspired by Karpathy's LLM Wiki. Three-layer raw/wiki/schema architecture, persistent markdown wiki, knowledge graph, hybrid SQLite FTS + embeddings, contradiction detection, and a built-in MCP server. MIT.

summary.one_liner: SwarmVault is a local-first CLI that compiles raw documents, code, and URLs into a persistent markdown wiki, a knowledge graph, and a hybrid search index that AI agents can query.
summary.what_it_does: Ingests local files, directories, public GitHub repos, URLs, transcripts, email, spreadsheets, and many other formats into an immutable raw/ folder, then compiles them into generated markdown wiki pages with a typed knowledge graph (edges tagged extracted, inferred, or ambiguous). It provides hybrid retrieval combining SQLite full-text search with optional embeddings, plus graph queries such as query, path, explain, and callers. It flags contradictions, stages changes into reviewable approval bundles, and writes context packs and task-ledger records for agents. An MCP server (swarmvault mcp) and per-agent install targets expose the vault to coding agents. The default heuristic provider runs offline without API keys, and Ollama or cloud LLM providers can be configured for sharper extraction.
use_cases: Build a personal knowledge base from notes, papers, and articles
Document a code repository with a navigable knowledge graph
Give coding agents bounded, cited context about a codebase
Turn meeting recordings and transcripts into searchable wiki pages
Query accumulated research with local search and saved answers
Audit a body of documents for conflicting claims
how_to_run: swarmvault query "What are the key concepts?"
notable: Three-layer raw/wiki/schema architecture modeled on Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern
Runs fully offline with a built-in heuristic provider and no API keys
Knowledge graph with provenance tags and graph report pages
Built-in MCP server and install targets for many coding agents
Approval bundles and candidate pages so generated changes are reviewed before landing
caveats: Requires Node.js 24 or newer for the CLI; a desktop app is offered as an alternative
Some features need external helpers or providers, such as ffmpeg/yt-dlp for video and whisper.cpp or hosted APIs for audio
Output quality is much sharper with an LLM provider than with the offline heuristic provider
The local-whisper provider is documented as experimental
